newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish short-end spreads still high, outlook down.
newsitem.headline: Spanish short-end spreads still high, outlook down.

text.p: Spanish Secretary of the Economy Cristobal Montoro said on Friday that despite narrowing yield spreads for bonds, the differential for short-term Spanish issues over German ones remains high and should decline.
"The spreads at the short end continue to be high compared with spreads at the long end," Montoro told Reuters in an interview.

Short-end spreads over equivalent German issues are at some 200 basis points in the two- and three-year maturities, while at the long end, bonos against Bunds, the spread has dipped to about 90 basis points currently from 330 last March.
Montoro said the spread would narrow as the Spanish economy managed to reduce its "basic disequilibriums" and amid expectations of bigger falls in inflation and in the deficit.

"As inflation moderates and there are visible and tough controls on the public deficit, the outlook for short-term rates is also downward," Montoro said. "I understand that this is the outlook on which the market is betting."
